title: Government and RBI Strengthen Digital Lending Ecosystem Through New Regulatory Framework, Digital Lending App Directory and Enhanced Customer Safeguards
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Finance Government and RBI Strengthen Digital Lending Ecosystem Through New Regulatory Framework, Digital Lending App Directory and Enhanced Customer Safeguards Initiatives include RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, Engagements with the major internet intermediaries, I4C, ‘SACHET’ portal, among others to proactively analyse digital lending apps प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 JUL 2026 5:41PM by PIB Delhi The Government has been constantly engaging with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and other concerned Regulators/stakeholders to curb the operations of fake/illegal loan apps in the country. For public information, RBI has operationalized a directory ‘Digital Lending Apps (DLAs)’ on its website with effect from 01.07.2025, including DLAs engaged by Regulated Entities (REs) of RBI. The directory aims to aid the customers in verifying the claim of a DLA’s association with a RE. Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has so far blocked a total of 87 illegal loan lending applications under section 69A of the Information Technology Act 2000 after following the due process. Additionally, sectoral regulators have been authorised to issue directions for blocking of information for public access under the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2025, notified on 22.10.2025 Further, the Government and RBI have been taking up various initiatives from time to time to protect citizens from exploitation by fake/illegal loan apps. These inter-alia, includes: RBI has issued Reserve Bank of India (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025 on May 8, 2025. These directions have detailed provision regarding recovery, data privacy, and customer grievance redressal mechanisms which are mandatory for the REs, the Lending Service Providers (LSPs) engaged by them and the Digital Lending Apps (DLAs). The Government and RBI have been proactively engaging with the major internet intermediaries and messaging platforms to review the operations of unauthorised loan apps. i Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has been proactively analysing the digital lending apps. In order to facilitate the citizens to report cyber incidents including fake/illegal loan apps, MHA has launched a National Cybercrime Reporting Portal (www.cybercrime.gov.in) as well as a National Cybercrime Helpline number “1930”. The banks through the public facing platform ‘SACHET’ portal and the State Level Coordination Committee (SLCC) facilitate the citizens for lodging of any complaints against specific entity related to deposit/ collection of money illegally. RBI and banks have been taking up awareness campaigns through short SMS, radio campaign, publicity on prevention of ‘cyber-crime’. Further, RBI has been conducting electronic-banking awareness and training (e-BAAT) programmes which focuses on awareness about frauds and risk mitigation. This information was given by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance Shri Pankaj Chaudhary in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today. *** SR/AD (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287195) आगंतुक पटल  : 155 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati Ministry of Finance Government and RBI Strengthen Digital Lending Ecosystem Through New Regulatory Framework, Digital Lending App Directory and Enhanced Customer Safeguards Initiatives include RBI (Digital Lending) Directions, 2025, Engagements with the major internet intermediaries, I4C, ‘SACHET’ portal, among others to proactively analyse digital lending apps प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
title: Government Strengthens Dairy and Livestock Sector Through Infrastructure, Digital Reforms and Veterinary Services
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Government Strengthens Dairy and Livestock Sector Through Infrastructure, Digital Reforms and Veterinary Services प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 JUL 2026 4:19PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh, informed the Lok Sabha that the Government is implementing several initiatives to strengthen India’s dairy and livestock sector by expanding infrastructure, improving veterinary healthcare, promoting digital livestock management and supporting dairy farmers. 1. No Proposal for Minimum Support Price (MSP) for Milk Replying to a question on milk pricing, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh stated that there is no proposal to introduce a Minimum Support Price (MSP) for milk. He explained that milk prices are determined by dairy cooperatives and private dairies based on market conditions. The Minister highlighted that the Government continues to support dairy farmers through various schemes aimed at increasing milk procurement, expanding processing capacity, strengthening village-level dairy cooperative societies, improving milk quality testing facilities and creating modern dairy infrastructure across the country. 2. AHIDF Boosting Livestock Infrastructure and Farmer Income Responding to a question on the Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF), Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh said that the scheme is promoting investment in dairy processing, meat processing, animal feed plants and value-addition infrastructure. The Minister informed the House that the Department regularly conducts awareness programmes, stakeholder meetings, training sessions and outreach activities through State Governments, Common Service Centres and industry associations to ensure wider participation. He added that the infrastructure created under AHIDF is improving market access and helping livestock farmers obtain better returns for their produce. 3. National Digital Livestock Mission Ensuring Secure Digital Animal Identification Replying to a question on the National Digital Livestock Mission (NDLM), Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh said that every registered animal is assigned a unique 12-digit Tag ID, enabling digital recording of vaccination, breeding, treatment and other veterinary services throughout the animal’s life. The Minister stated that the portal uses AES-256 encryption and Transport Layer Security (TLS) to ensure government-grade protection of livestock data. He also informed the House that Mobile Veterinary Units are not yet integrated with the portal and no request for banking API integration has been received so far. 4. Dairy Development Initiatives Expanding Across the Country Answering a question on dairy development, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh said that the Government is implementing several flagship programmes to enhance milk production, improve farmers’ incomes and generate rural employment. The Minister highlighted that schemes such as the National Livestock Mission (NLM), Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP) and Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) are supporting entrepreneurship, breed improvement, disease control, veterinary infrastructure and affordable veterinary medicines. He further informed that 113 AHIDF projects worth ₹4,700.13 crore have been approved in Maharashtra , with interest subvention of ₹123.46 crore released. *** SM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287066) आगंतुक पटल  : 152 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Gujarati Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Government Strengthens Dairy and Livestock Sector Through Infrastructure, Digital Reforms and Veterinary Services प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
title: Mangaluru Fishing Harbour
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Mangaluru Fishing Harbour प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 JUL 2026 3:09PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF,GoI), regularly reviews the implementation of projects approved under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) in all States/Union Territories(UTs) including Karnataka through physical meetings, virtual meetings, field visits and the digital monitoring through a dedicated centralized digital platform for scheme implementation. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India approved the proposal of the Government of Karnataka for Modernisation and Upgradation of Mangalore Fishing Harbour in 2024 at a cost of Rs 37.47 Crore with central share of Rs 22.48 Crore under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). The Department of Fisheries, Government of India has released Rs 126.01 Crore for fisheries development projects in State of Karnataka from 2023-24 to 2026-27. This also takes into account the funds for fishing harbour infrastructure including the project of Modernisation and Upgradation of Mangalore Fishing Harbour. The State Government of Karnataka has reported a physical progress of 25% and expenditure of Rs 6.31 Crore in the Mangalore Fishing Harbour project. The project was envisaged to facilitate berthing facilities for 1600 fishing vessels and to benefit about 18000 fishers and associated stakeholders in the fisheries sector.The Government of Karnataka has reported that the pending components in the project of the Modernization and Upgradation of Mangalore Fishing Harbour project is scheduled to be completed by 21st May, 2027. Under PMMSY, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India approved various fisheries development projects in the State of Karnataka at a total cost of Rs 1,053.60 crore from 2020-21 to 2026-2027, which are at various stages of implementation. Under PMMSY, the selection of beneficiaries is carried out by the respective State Government. Accordingly, the Government of Karnataka reported that 212 beneficiaries in the three coastal districts of Karnataka were covered under beneficiary-oriented activities, including deep-sea fishing vessels, ice plants, cold storages, refrigerated vehicles, insulated vehicles, three-wheelers with ice boxes, and motorcycles with ice boxes. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India has taken several measures under PMMSY to address infrastructure and operational requirements of the fisheries sector, including development and modernization of fishing harbours and fish landing centres, cold chain infrastructure, hygienic fish handling facilities, fish transport and marketing infrastructure, quality fish seed production, access to institutional credit through the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) and Kisan Credit Card (KCC), strengthening of aquatic animal health and biosecurity measures, promotion of insurance coverage, and capacity building of fishers. This information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked. *** JP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287001) आगंतुक पटल  : 127 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Kannada Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Mangaluru Fishing Harbour प्रविष्टि तिथि:

The project was envisaged to facilitate berthing facilities for 1600 fishing vessels and to benefit about 18000 fishers and associated stakeholders in the fisheries sector.The Government of Karnataka has reported that the pending components in the project of the Modernization and Upgradation of Mangalore Fishing Harbour project is scheduled to be completed by 21st May, 2027. Under PMMSY, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India approved various fisheries development projects in the State of Karnataka at a total cost of Rs 1,053.60 crore from 2020-21 to 2026-2027, which are at various stages of implementation. Under PMMSY, the selection of beneficiaries is carried out by the respective State Government. Accordingly, the Government of Karnataka reported that 212 beneficiaries in the three coastal districts of Karnataka were covered under beneficiary-oriented activities, including deep-sea fishing vessels, ice plants, cold storages, refrigerated vehicles, insulated vehicles, three-wheelers with ice boxes, and motorcycles with ice boxes. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India has taken several measures under PMMSY to address infrastructure and operational requirements of the fisheries sector, including development and modernization of fishing harbours and fish landing centres, cold chain infrastructure, hygienic fish handling facilities, fish transport and marketing infrastructure, quality fish seed production, access to institutional credit through the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) and Kisan Credit Card (KCC), strengthening of aquatic animal health and biosecurity measures, promotion of insurance coverage, and capacity building of fishers. This information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked. *** JP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287001)

title: Coastal Fishing Village
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Coastal Fishing Village प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 JUL 2026 3:06PM by PIB Delhi The PMMSY, implemented from 2020-21, provides for developing Integrated Modern Coastal Villages at a unit cost of ₹750 lakh to enhance economic and social gains for coastal fishers through sustainable practices. The initiative strengthens livelihoods and participation across the fisheries value chain by supporting modern infrastructure, disaster-resilient housing, cyclone and tsunami shelters, and post-harvest amenities tailored to local needs. It is a non-beneficiary-oriented intervention implemented jointly with coastal State Governments on a 60:40 cost-sharing basis. The scheme leverages the inherent strengths of coastal communities to promote sustainable economic growth. The Government of Andhra Pradesh has not availed this activity under the PMMSY. The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, recognizing the importance of developing the coastal communities, has also taken up another transformative initiative under the Pradhan Mantri Matya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) to develop the existing 100 fishermen villages situated close to the coastline in various States and Union Territories (UTs), including Andhra Pradesh, into Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages (CRCFV), to make them economically vibrant fishermen villages. The development of CRCFV has been taken up under the Central Sector scheme component of the PMMSY with a unit cost of Rs 200 lakh per fishing village, and the entire cost (100%) is borne by the Government of India. The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, in consultation with the Government of Andhra Pradesh, has identified 15 villages in the state for development as CRCFV, including Sorlagondhi and Gullalamodha in Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh. The proposals of the Government of Andhra Pradesh to develop the identified 15 villages as CRCFV at a total cost of Rs. 30 crore have been approved based on the Detailed Project Report (DPR) submitted by the State, and so far, Rs. 15.0 Crore has been released to the Government of Andhra Pradesh for implementation of the approved projects of CRCFV based on the utilisation. The approved interventions for Sorlagondhi and Gullalamodha villages include fish-drying platforms, solar fish-drying units, multipurpose fisheries center, common fish market, high-mast solar lights, and jetty extension for safe boat mooring. Livelihood and climate-resilient activities comprise seaweed culture farms, sea-cage culture, colour GPS units, life-saving appliances, iceboxes, and other productivity-enhancing assets. The details of the interventions in both villages are provided in Annexure I. title: FFPOs under PMMSY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying FFPOs under PMMSY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 JUL 2026 3:05PM by PIB Delhi The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) implemented by the Department of Fisheries, Government of India inter-alia provides financial assistance for setting up of Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPOs) to economically empower the fishers, fish farmers and enhance their bargaining power. The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying during the last five years (FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26) has approved projects worth of Rs.544.86 crore for formation of 2195 FFPOs including formation of 195 new FFPOs and formation of 2000 existing Primary Fisheries Cooperative Societies(PFCSs) as FFPOs in the country. This project is implemented through four central agencies namely National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB), Small Farmers Agri-business Consortium (SFAC), National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India (NAFED) and National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC). It is reported that so far a total 2104 Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPOs) have been formed in the country including 192 FFPOs in the State of Andhra Pradesh. The State-wise details of the Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPOs) formed in the country under PMMSY as on date are furnished at Annexure-I. It is reported that 10 new Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPOs) have been formed and registered in Andhra Pradesh with a Government support of Rs 328.20 lakh under the PMMSY. The supports extended to such newly formed FFPOs include incubation, management cost and equity grant. The district-wise details of the newly formed FFPOs in Andhra Pradesh are furnished at Annexure-II. In addition, 182 existing Primary Fisheries Cooperative Societies(PFCSs) have been formed as Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPOs) at a total investment of Rs 963.73 lakh covering management cost and equity grant in the State of Andhra Pradesh. This includes formation of 34 primary fisheries cooperatives as FFPO at a cost of Rs. 165.82 lakh in Konaseema District of Andhra Pradesh. The District-wise details of these 182 existing primary fisheries cooperatives formed as FFPO in the State of Andhra Pradesh under PMMSY are furnished at Annexure-III. It is reported that a total 39,022 members are associated with aforementioned 192 functional FFPOs including 6136 members in new FFPOs and remaining 32,886 members of existing PFCSs formed as FFPOs in the State of Andhra Pradesh. This information was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Lok Sabha in response to a question asked. ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
title: Registered Fishermen Families
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Registered Fishermen Families प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 JUL 2026 3:04PM by PIB Delhi As per the information received from Government of Tamil Nadu, a total number of 1,480 inland fish farmers are registered with the District Fish Farmers Development Agency (DFFDA) and a total number of 1,234 inland fishermen  are registered in inland fishermen cooperative societies in Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu. Funds to the tune of  Rs. 196.30 Lakhs have been disbursed under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), during the last three years (2021-22 to 2023-24) for the implementation of the projects namely construction of freshwater finfish hatchery (2 units), construction of seed rearing ponds (07 ha), construction of new grow out ponds and input assistance (25 ha), input subsidy assistance for grow out ponds (25 ha), establishment of small Biofloc units (09 units) and establishment of re-circulatory aquaculture system (01 unit). (b) As informed by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) the Central Inland Fisheries Research Institute (CIFRI) has conducted a study in the Cauvery River stretch in Thanjavur District, Tamil Nadu. The study revealed that extensive diversion of river water for agricultural purposes through a well-developed canal network has resulted in reduced flow in this stretch for most of the year. The river stretch receives water mainly during the monsoon season and through regulated releases from upstream reservoirs. Consequently, riverine capture fisheries in the Thanjavur stretch remain seasonal, with limited intensity. Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) implemented by the Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI), the River Ranching Programme was implemented in Tamil Nadu, under which 176 lakh advanced fingerlings were released in river stretches across the State (including 59.76 lakh in Cauvery riverine system) to enhance fishery resources and conserve native fish biodiversity, enhance fish catches and protect the livelihood of inland fishers. This stocking is anticipated to increase the fish production to 220 tonnes in the Cauvery river system thereby enhancing inland fish production and supporting the livelihood of inland fishers. (c) The DoF, GoI since 2015, has substantially stepped-up investment in fisheries sector through various schemes for holistic development of fisheries, inland aquaculture and welfare of fishermen in the country including delta districts of Tamil Nadu (Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurai and Cuddalore). The Government of Tamil Nadu has implemented several activities under the PMMSY and the state schemes to enhance the fish production, area expansion under aquaculture, promotion of sustainable livelihoods and intensive aquaculture by adopting technologies such as Biofloc Systems and Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS). In addition, subsidy assistance is provided under the PMMSY for fishing gear to reduce the operational costs of inland fishers. The Government of Tamil Nadu has informed that subsidy assistance under PMMSY has been provided to 355 beneficiaries from Delta districts for activities such as input assistance and construction of freshwater finfish hatcheries, new seed rearing ponds, grow out ponds, establishment of Biofloc units, RAS, ornamental units, and purchase of fishing gear. The State has also facilitated the stocking of 9.00 lakh fingerlings in Panchayat tanks covering an area of 450 hectares across the Delta districts during 2024–25 and 2025–26.                         21 JUL 2026 3:04PM by PIB Delhi As per the information received from Government of Tamil Nadu, a total number of 1,480 inland fish farmers are registered with the District Fish Farmers Development Agency (DFFDA) and a total number of 1,234 inland fishermen  are registered in inland fishermen cooperative societies in Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu. Funds to the tune of  Rs. 196.30 Lakhs have been disbursed under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), during the last three years (2021-22 to 2023-24) for the implementation of the projects namely construction of freshwater finfish hatchery (2 units), construction of seed rearing ponds (07 ha), construction of new grow out ponds and input assistance (25 ha), input subsidy assistance for grow out ponds (25 ha), establishment of small Biofloc units (09 units) and establishment of re-circulatory aquaculture system (01 unit). (b) As informed by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) the Central Inland Fisheries Research Institute (CIFRI) has conducted a study in the Cauvery River stretch in Thanjavur District, Tamil Nadu. The study revealed that extensive diversion of river water for agricultural purposes through a well-developed canal network has resulted in reduced flow in this stretch for most of the year. The river stretch receives water mainly during the monsoon season and through regulated releases from upstream reservoirs. Consequently, riverine capture fisheries in the Thanjavur stretch remain seasonal, with limited intensity. Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) implemented by the Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI), the River Ranching Programme was implemented in Tamil Nadu, under which 176 lakh advanced fingerlings were released in river stretches across the State (including 59.76 lakh in Cauvery riverine system) to enhance fishery resources and conserve native fish biodiversity, enhance fish catches and protect the livelihood of inland fishers. This stocking is anticipated to increase the fish production to 220 tonnes in the Cauvery river system thereby enhancing inland fish production and supporting the livelihood of inland fishers. (c) The DoF, GoI since 2015, has substantially stepped-up investment in fisheries sector through various schemes for holistic development of fisheries, inland aquaculture and welfare of fishermen in the country including delta districts of Tamil Nadu (Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurai and Cuddalore). The Government of Tamil Nadu has implemented several activities under the PMMSY and the state schemes to enhance the fish production, area expansion under aquaculture, promotion of sustainable livelihoods and intensive aquaculture by adopting technologies such as Biofloc Systems and Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS). In addition, subsidy assistance is provided under the PMMSY for fishing gear to reduce the operational costs of inland fishers. Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Fish Production प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 JUL 2026 3:03PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India with effect from the Financial Year 2020-21 is implementing the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) for holistic development of fisheries and aquaculture sector in the country. This scheme during its implementation period of last six years has made vital contribution towards augmentation of fish production in the country. During the period of the PMMSY, the fish production in the country has increased from 141.64 lakh tonne (2019-20) to 197.75 lakh tonne (2024-25). (b):      The PMMSY inter-alia encompasses inclusive development by providing higher financial assistance of 60 percent of the unit cost for women beneficiaries under beneficiary-oriented activities. Under the PMMSY, during the last six Financial Years (2020-21 to 2025-26), fisheries development proposals amounting to Rs.4178.30 crore have been sanctioned for covering a total 1,47,654 women beneficiaries across various States and Union Territories. (c) & (d):         Development of cold chain and marketing infrastructure facilities for fisheries and aquaculture is one of the thrust areas of the central schemes implemented by the Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying.  The Department of Fisheries, Government of India till April, 2026 has accorded approvals to the proposals amounting to Rs 2,797 crore under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) and Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) for development of cold chain and marketing facilities in the country. The key activities approved includes; 775 cold storages and ice plants, 28,489 units of fish transportation facilities such as 13,718 motorcycles with ice boxes, 8,527 bicycles with ice boxes, 4,257 auto rickshaws, 1,577 insulated trucks and 410 refrigerated trucks, 1,394 live fish vending units, 6,018 fish kiosks, 117 retail fish markets, 24 wholesale fish markets in all the States and Union Territories.                 21 JUL 2026 2:59PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (MoFAH&D), Government of India, is implementing a range of schemes and programmes for the holistic development of the fisheries and aquaculture sector across the country, including Balasore District of Odisha based on the proposal and recommendations received from the State Governments. Over the last twelve years, from 2014‑15 onwards, under the Blue Revolution (BR) and Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), the DoF has approved proposals of the Government of Odisha amounting to a total project cost of ₹1,567.96 crore, with a Central share of ₹549.58 crore, for fisheries and aquaculture development in the State, including Balasore District. Further, under the Fisheries and Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), 13 projects with a total cost of ₹784.32 crore and a restricted interest subvention of ₹286.39 crore have been approved for Odisha. Of these, 2 projects costing ₹8.26 crore have been sanctioned for implementation in Balasore District. The Government of Odisha has also informed that the Mukhyamantri Matsyajibi Kalyan Yojana (MMKY) is being implemented by the State Government for the development of the fisheries and aquaculture sector across Odisha, including Balasore District. The major activities undertaken in Balasore District under the Blue Revolution (BR) and the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) during 2014‑15 to 2025‑26 include the development of the Chandipur Fishing Harbour at a cost of ₹49.94 crore; establishment of a State‑of‑the‑Art Wholesale Fish Market at Basta at a cost of ₹78.20 crore; development of five Climate Resilient Coastal Fishermen Villages (CRCFV); installation of six cold storage/ice plant units; implementation of sea cage culture demonstration of Indian pompano at Bahabalpur coast at a cost of ₹2.57 crore; bringing 107 hectares of brackish‑water area under aquaculture; and establishment of three finfish hatcheries and one scampi hatchery. Additionally, Balasore has been declared the Production and Processing Cluster of Scampi. As reported by the Government of Odisha, a total allocation of ₹250.71 crore has been made for Balasore district since 2014‑15 under various fisheries development schemes, of which ₹214.45 crore (86%) has been utilized. content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare India to Host the Sixteenth BRICS Health Ministers' Meeting in Chandigarh from 22–24 July Three-Day BRICS Health Programme to Feature Senior Officials' Meeting, Health Ministers' Meeting and Dialogue on Digital Health & AI Union Health Secretary and Secretary, Ministry of Ayush Brief Media on Preparations for the Sixteenth BRICS Health Ministers' Meeting India's BRICS Chairship Guided by Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability Nine Priority Areas to Guide BRICS Health Cooperation under India's Chairship Health Ministerial Declaration to Reinforce BRICS Commitment to Global Health प्रविष्टि तिथि:

Ahead of the Ministerial Meeting, a press conference was held in Chandigarh today, where Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Union Health Secretary, Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and Shri Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, briefed the media on the preparations, agenda and expected outcomes of the Sixteenth BRICS Health Ministers' Meeting. ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: BRICS Nations Join Hands to strengthen TCIM, Expert Working Group Taking Shape
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare BRICS Nations Join Hands to strengthen TCIM, Expert Working Group Taking Shape Delegates immersed themselves in Ayush through Ayush Zone, experienced Ayush Aahar, health and wellness consultations and India's herbal heritage प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 JUL 2026 5:14PM by PIB Delhi India successfully hosted the BRICS Meeting on Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine (TCIM) on 21 July 2026 at Chandigarh, as part of its BRICS 2026 Chairship. The meeting formed part of the broader four-day programme of BRICS Health Track events in Chandigarh, jointly organised by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the Ministry of Ayush. The TCIM meeting brought together senior government officials, technical experts and delegates from BRICS member countries to strengthen multilateral cooperation, promote the exchange of knowledge and best practices, and advance collaboration in the field of Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine. Held under the overarching BRICS Chairship theme, "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation & Sustainability," the meeting advanced collaboration among BRICS nations to promote evidence-based traditional medicine systems, strengthen institutional partnerships and contribute towards sustainable and resilient healthcare systems. The meeting witnessed participation from the BRICS member states—Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Iran, Russia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates—providing a platform to exchange best practices, policy experiences and scientific advancements in Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine. The formal proceedings on TCIM commenced with a welcome address by Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, followed by opening remarks from member delegations. The Terms of Reference (ToR) for the proposed BRICS Expert Working Group on TCIM were finalised with the consensus of all available member states. The meeting also featured interactive discussions on strengthening collaboration, harmonising policy approaches and identifying future areas of cooperation among BRICS nations. A dedicated side event on "Capacity Building, Education and Human Resource Development" was also organised by the Ministry of Ayush. The session focused on strengthening global education and training in traditional medicine through academic collaborations, Ayush scholarship initiatives, faculty and student exchanges, research partnerships and evidence-generation mechanisms aimed at building a globally connected TCIM ecosystem. As part of India's BRICS Chairship 2026, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, also inaugurated the Ayush Zone, showcasing India's holistic healthcare initiatives. The Ayush Zone offered BRICS delegates an immersive experience of Ayush through Ayush Aahar, health and wellness consultations, India's herbal heritage, the Ministry's vision and global initiatives, and a dedicated hub on research, innovation and knowledge. Featuring wellness activities and Yoga, the Ayush Zone reflected India's commitment to fostering international collaboration in Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine. The TCIM deliberations contributed to the broader BRICS Health Track led by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and supported ongoing discussions on strengthening healthcare cooperation among BRICS countries. The four-day programme also features a range of wellness and cultural activities showcasing India's holistic healthcare traditions. Delegates participated in Chair Yoga sessions, and will engage in Common Yoga Protocol (CYP) demonstrations organised by the Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga (MDNIY), Yoga Break (Y-Break) sessions during meetings, and the Fit India Run. The Ayush Zone, along with the Ayush Aahar Mela curated with technical support from the National Institute of Ayurveda (NIA), showcased India's traditional healthcare ecosystem through health and wellness consultations, research and innovation exhibits, live Yoga demonstrations and other wellness activities, providing delegates with a comprehensive experience of the country's holistic healthcare traditions. The meeting delivered several significant outcomes, including progress towards the establishment of a BRICS Expert Working Group on Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine; enhanced cooperation in research, education and regulatory frameworks; improved knowledge-sharing among member countries; and stronger recognition of Traditional, Complementary and Integrative Medicine within the BRICS Health agenda. The BRICS TCIM Meeting reflected India's continued commitment to promoting evidence-based traditional medicine, fostering international partnerships and advancing holistic, accessible and sustainable healthcare for all. *** SR (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287153) आगंतुक पटल  : 170 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Gujarati , हिन्दी Ministry of Health and Family Welfare BRICS Nations Join Hands to strengthen TCIM, Expert Working Group Taking Shape Delegates immersed themselves in Ayush through Ayush Zone, experienced Ayush Aahar, health and wellness consultations and India's herbal heritage प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Steps Taken to Strengthen Primary Healthcare Services in the country
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Steps Taken to Strengthen Primary Healthcare Services in the country Under NP-NCD, 770 District NCD Clinics, 524 Day Care Cancer Centres, 233 Cardiac Care Units and 6410 Community Health Centre NCD Clinics has been set up Through 1.86 lakh AAMs, comprehensive primary healthcare is provided by strengthening Sub Health Centres and Primary Health Centres AB PM-JAY scheme has been expanded to cover 6 crore senior citizens of age 70 years and above belonging to 4.5 crore families irrespective of their socio-economic status प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 JUL 2026 2:01PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare provides technical and financial support to the States/UTs to strengthen the public healthcare services and to promote disease prevention, based on the proposals received in the form of Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) under National Health Mission (NHM). Government of India provides approval for the proposals in the form of Record of Proceedings (RoPs) as per norms & available resources. Various initiatives carried out under NHM by the Government of India in the country are operationalization of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs), Free Drugs Service Initiative, Free Diagnostic Service Initiative, National Ambulance Services, Mobile Medical Units, ASHAs, 24 x 7 Services and First Referral Facilities, Prime Minister's National Dialysis Programme, various activities under Reproductive & Child Health, Anaemia Mukt Bharat (AMB) strategy, TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan and Universal Immunization programme. National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD) focuses on strengthening infrastructure, human resource development, early diagnosis, referral to an appropriate level of healthcare facility for treatment and management and health promotion and awareness generation for prevention of NCDs including cervical cancer. Under NP-NCD, 770 District NCD Clinics, 524 Day Care Cancer Centres, 233 Cardiac Care Units and 6410 Community Health Centre NCD Clinics has been set up. A population-based initiative for screening, management and prevention of common NCDs has been rolled out as a part of comprehensive Primary Health Care in the country under NHM. Through 1.86 lakh AAMs, comprehensive primary healthcare is provided by strengthening Sub Health Centres (SHCs) and Primary Health Centres (PHCs) . These AAMs provide preventive, promotive, rehabilitative and curative care for an expanded range of services encompassing reproductive and child healthcare services, Communicable diseases, Non-communicable diseases and other health issues. Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri - Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) is a flagship scheme of the Government which provides health cover of Rs. 5 lakhs per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization to approximately 55 Crore beneficiaries corresponding to 12.37 Crore families constituting economically vulnerable bottom 40% of India’s population. Recently, the scheme has been expanded to cover 6 crore senior citizens of age 70 years and above belonging to 4.5 crore families irrespective of their socio-economic status under AB PM-JAY with Vay Vandana Card. Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) aims to create an online platform enabling interoperability of health data within the health ecosystem to create longitudinal electronic health record of every citizen, make healthcare accessible for citizens. The teleconsultation services, available at all operational AAMs across the country, enables people to access the specialist services closer to their homes addressing concerns of physical accessibility, shortage of service providers and to facilitate continuum of care. PM-Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM), launched with an outlay of Rs. 64,180 crores, focuses on developing capacities of health systems and institutions across the country. The Government of India has undertaken various initiatives under NHM to improve maternal, neonatal and child health outcomes across the country. Key measures are as follows: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) and Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakaram (JSSK): Promote institutional deliveries and provide free, cashless delivery (including caesarean), diagnostics, drugs, diet, transport and blood transfusion in public health facilities, with similar benefits for sick infants. Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA): Provides free, assured antenatal check-ups by Specialists/Medical Officers on the 9th of every month, with emphasis on identification and management of high-risk pregnancies. Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan (SUMAN): Ensures assured, dignified, respectful and quality healthcare at no cost with zero tolerance for denial of services to pregnant women and newborns. Postnatal Care Initiatives: Strengthen early detection, referral and management of high-risk postpartum mothers through ASHA support. Anemia Mukt Bharat (AMB): Addresses anemia among children, adolescents, women of reproductive age, pregnant and lactating women through a lifecycle approach. Nutrition and Child Health Interventions: Include Mothers’ Absolute Affection (MAA), Lactation Management Centres, Vitamin A supplementation, Home-Based Newborn Care (HBNC)/Home-Based Care for Young Child Programme (HBYC) and Mission Poshan 2.0. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. *** SR HFW / PQ-Steps taken to strengthen Primary Healthcare Services/21 July 2026/2 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2286956) आगंतुक पटल  : 206 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Steps Taken to Strengthen Primary Healthcare Services in the country Under NP-NCD, 770 District NCD Clinics, 524 Day Care Cancer Centres, 233 Cardiac Care Units and 6410 Community Health Centre NCD Clinics has been set up Through 1.86 lakh AAMs, comprehensive primary healthcare is provided by strengthening Sub Health Centres and Primary Health Centres AB PM-JAY scheme has been expanded to cover 6 crore senior citizens of age 70 years and above belonging to 4.5 crore families irrespective of their socio-economic status प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Steps Taken to Enhance National Preparedness against Emerging Infectious Diseases
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Steps Taken to Enhance National Preparedness against Emerging Infectious Diseases Nationwide VRDL Network under ICMR has been expanded to 163 laboratories, comprising 11 Regional VRDLs, 27 State VRDLs and 125 Medical College VRDLs, to strengthen diagnostic capacity across the country Infectious Disease Research and Diagnostic Laboratories and four Regional Next-Generation Sequencing Hubs have been established to enhance decentralized diagnostics, genomic characterization of pathogens, standardized data generation and timely reporting Coordination mechanisms between Central and State health authorities during public health emergencies have been strengthened and tested through simulation exercises and mock drills प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 JUL 2026 1:59PM by PIB Delhi The Union Health Ministry regularly reviews and strengthens its preparedness for the detection and response to emerging infectious diseases through various national programs and institutions including the Viral Research and Diagnostic Laboratories (VRDL) network, genomic surveillance initiatives and wastewater surveillance for early detection of pathogens of public health importance. The preparedness is further strengthened through participation in simulation exercises, mock drills and rapid outbreak response mechanisms. The Ministry through the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) is implementing Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP) which is mandated with surveillance & response to outbreak prone communicable diseases. The nationwide VRDL Network under the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has been expanded to 163 laboratories, comprising 11 Regional VRDLs, 27 State VRDLs and 125 Medical College VRDLs, to strengthen diagnostic capacity across the country. In addition, Infectious Disease Research and Diagnostic Laboratories and four Regional Next-Generation Sequencing Hubs have been established to enhance decentralized diagnostics, genomic characterization of pathogens, standardized data generation and timely reporting to support public health surveillance and outbreak response. Coordination between Central and State health authorities during public health emergencies has been strengthened through real-time disease surveillance and reporting under the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP)/Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP), regular information sharing, and coordinated outbreak response mechanisms. During outbreaks, the Ministry extends technical support through collaborative outbreak investigations, risk assessment, laboratory confirmation, and deployment of multidisciplinary experts under the National Joint Outbreak Response Team, as required. Coordination mechanisms between Central and State health authorities during public health emergencies have also been tested through simulation exercises and mock drills. As a part of a comprehensive approach to manage future public health emergencies, Pradhan Mantri - Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) has been launched with the intent to enhance the capacity of primary, secondary and tertiary health care facilities/systems and institutes for identifying and managing any new and emerging diseases. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. *** SR HFW / PQ - Steps taken to Strengthen Infectious Disease Preparedness/21 July 2026/5 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2286953) आगंतुक पटल  : 130 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Bengali , Tamil Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Steps Taken to Enhance National Preparedness against Emerging Infectious Diseases Nationwide VRDL Network under ICMR has been expanded to 163 laboratories, comprising 11 Regional VRDLs, 27 State VRDLs and 125 Medical College VRDLs, to strengthen diagnostic capacity across the country Infectious Disease Research and Diagnostic Laboratories and four Regional Next-Generation Sequencing Hubs have been established to enhance decentralized diagnostics, genomic characterization of pathogens, standardized data generation and timely reporting Coordination mechanisms between Central and State health authorities during public health emergencies have been strengthened and tested through simulation exercises and mock drills प्रविष्टि तिथि:

The nationwide VRDL Network under the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has been expanded to 163 laboratories, comprising 11 Regional VRDLs, 27 State VRDLs and 125 Medical College VRDLs, to strengthen diagnostic capacity across the country. In addition, Infectious Disease Research and Diagnostic Laboratories and four Regional Next-Generation Sequencing Hubs have been established to enhance decentralized diagnostics, genomic characterization of pathogens, standardized data generation and timely reporting to support public health surveillance and outbreak response. Coordination between Central and State health authorities during public health emergencies has been strengthened through real-time disease surveillance and reporting under the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP)/Integrated Health Information Platform (IHIP), regular information sharing, and coordinated outbreak response mechanisms. During outbreaks, the Ministry extends technical support through collaborative outbreak investigations, risk assessment, laboratory confirmation, and deployment of multidisciplinary experts under the National Joint Outbreak Response Team, as required. Coordination mechanisms between Central and State health authorities during public health emergencies have also been tested through simulation exercises and mock drills. As a part of a comprehensive approach to manage future public health emergencies, Pradhan Mantri - Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) has been launched with the intent to enhance the capacity of primary, secondary and tertiary health care facilities/systems and institutes for identifying and managing any new and emerging diseases. title: Update on Availability of Cancer Care Centres
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Update on Availability of Cancer Care Centres Under NP-NCD, 770 District NCD Clinics, 524 Day Care Cancer Centres and 6,410 NCD clinics at Community Health Centres have been set up across the country AB PM-JAY scheme covers cashless treatment for 1,961 procedures across 27 medical specialties, including Medical Oncology, Surgical Oncology and Radiation Oncology, through empanelled public and private hospitals To reduce waiting time for cancer diagnosis and treatment, population-based screening for common NCDs, including oral, breast and cervical cancers, is being undertaken under the National Health Mission Under the Strengthening of Tertiary Care Cancer Facilities Scheme, 19 State Cancer Institutes and 20 Tertiary Care Cancer Centres have been approved across the country Tata Memorial Centre has established six hospitals at Varanasi, Visakhapatnam, New Chandigarh, Guwahati, Sangrur and Muzaffarpur to provide comprehensive cancer care Cancer treatment services, including diagnostic, medical and surgical facilities have also been extended to all 22 new AIIMS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 JUL 2026 1:54PM by PIB Delhi Health being a State subject, the primary responsibility for providing healthcare services, including cancer care, rests with the respective State Governments. However, the Department of Health and Family Welfare provides technical and financial support to States and Union Territories across the country under the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD) as part of the National Health Mission (NHM). The programme focuses on strengthening infrastructure, human resource development, screening, early diagnosis, referral, treatment, and health promotion for Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs). Under NP-NCD, 770 District NCD Clinics, 524 Day Care Cancer Centres (DCCCs) and 6,410 NCD clinics at Community Health Centres have been set up across the country. Under Ayushman Bharat–Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY), eligible beneficiary families are provided health coverage of ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization. The scheme covers cashless treatment for 1,961 procedures across 27 medical specialties, including Medical Oncology, Surgical Oncology and Radiation Oncology, through empanelled public and private hospitals. States/UTs also have the flexibility to customize the Health Benefit Packages to address local healthcare needs. To reduce waiting periods for cancer diagnosis and treatment, population-based screening for common non-communicable diseases, including oral, breast and cervical cancers, is being undertaken under the National Health Mission (NHM) for individuals aged 30 years and above through Ayushman Arogya Mandirs by trained frontline health workers (ASHAs and ANMs). This facilitates early detection and timely referral, thereby reducing delays in diagnosis and initiation of treatment. Further, DCCCs are being established in District Hospitals under a hub-and-spoke model to decentralize cancer care and facilitate timely access to chemotherapy and other day-care oncology services. Under the Strengthening of Tertiary Care Cancer Facilities Scheme, 19 State Cancer Institutes (SCIs) and 20 Tertiary Care Cancer Centres (TCCCs) have been approved across the country to strengthen tertiary cancer care. Further, Tata Memorial Centre (TMC) has established six hospitals at Varanasi, Visakhapatnam, New Chandigarh, Guwahati, Sangrur and Muzaffarpur to provide comprehensive cancer care. Cancer treatment services, including diagnostic, medical and surgical facilities, have also been extended to all 22 new AIIMS. In addition, the National Cancer Institute (NCI), Jhajjar and the second campus of Chittaranjan National Cancer Institute (CNCI), Kolkata provide advanced diagnostic and treatment facilities. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav stated this in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. *** SR HFW / PQ-Update on Availability of Cancer Care Centres/21 July 2026/3 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2286948) आगंतुक पटल  : 135 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Update on Availability of Cancer Care Centres Under NP-NCD, 770 District NCD Clinics, 524 Day Care Cancer Centres and 6,410 NCD clinics at Community Health Centres have been set up across the country AB PM-JAY scheme covers cashless treatment for 1,961 procedures across 27 medical specialties, including Medical Oncology, Surgical Oncology and Radiation Oncology, through empanelled public and private hospitals To reduce waiting time for cancer diagnosis and treatment, population-based screening for common NCDs, including oral, breast and cervical cancers, is being undertaken under the National Health Mission Under the Strengthening of Tertiary Care Cancer Facilities Scheme, 19 State Cancer Institutes and 20 Tertiary Care Cancer Centres have been approved across the country Tata Memorial Centre has established six hospitals at Varanasi, Visakhapatnam, New Chandigarh, Guwahati, Sangrur and Muzaffarpur to provide comprehensive cancer care Cancer treatment services, including diagnostic, medical and surgical facilities have also been extended to all 22 new AIIMS प्रविष्टि तिथि:

content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Update on HPV Vaccination Programme and Cervical Cancer Prevention As of 15 July 2026, a total of 52,10,302 girls have received the HPV vaccine across the country Extensive training on HPV vaccination has been completed for medical and paramedical staff across all 36 States/UTs in the country A multi-faceted approach that includes HPV vaccination, screening, early diagnosis at Ayushman Arogya Mandirs and treatment through Day Care Cancer Centres is implemented by the Union Government against Cervical Cancer प्रविष्टि तिथि:

The extensive training on HPV vaccination has been completed for medical and paramedical staff across all 36 States/UTs in the country. ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: ICMR transfers three indigenous biomedical technologies to advance cancer and infectious disease solutions
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare ICMR transfers three indigenous biomedical technologies to advance cancer and infectious disease solutions SHetA2 Anti-HPV candidate, two enteric vaccines among technologies transferred for further development Technology transfer brings government-funded research closer to affordable healthcare Medical Innovations Patent Mitra driving India's path to self-reliance in healthcare innovation: Secretary DHR and DG ICMR, Dr. Rajiv Bahl प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 JUL 2026 11:26AM by PIB Delhi The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), under its Medical Innovations Patent Mitra initiative, facilitated the licensing of three indigenous biomedical technologies to leading Indian pharmaceutical and vaccine manufacturers for further development, manufacturing and commercialization. The technologies include SHetA2, a novel anti-HPV therapeutic candidate for the treatment of Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN), licensed to Emcure Pharmaceuticals Ltd., and two next-generation vaccine technologies against enteric bacterial infections, developed at ICMR–National Institute of Research in Bacterial Infections (ICMR-NIRBI), Kolkata, licensed to Biological E Ltd. These technology transfers mark another significant step towards accelerating the translation of publicly funded research into affordable healthcare solutions and strengthening India's biomedical innovation ecosystem. SHetA2, developed through a collaboration between Dr. Showket Hussain, ICMR National Institute of Cancer Prevention and Research (ICMR-NICPR) and Dr. Doris M. Benbrook, Stephenson Cancer Center, University of Oklahoma, USA, is a first-in-class targeted therapeutic candidate that selectively eliminates HPV-induced precancerous and cervical cancer cells while sparing healthy cells. The technology has the potential to provide a safe, affordable and minimally invasive treatment option for cervical cancer. The two vaccine technologies developed by Dr. Santasabuj Das and his team at ICMR National Institute for Research in Bacterial Infections (ICMR-NIRBI) include: A fusion construct containing Salmonella typhi outer membrane protein as a promising next-generation typhoid vaccine candidate. A recombinant vaccine composition against Salmonella typhi/paratyphi and Shigella infections, designed to provide broader protection against major enteric bacterial pathogens. Together, these technologies have the potential to strengthen India's efforts in cancer prevention and infectious disease control while advancing indigenous development of next-generation therapeutics and vaccines. Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Secretary, Department of Health Research (DHR) and Director General, ICMR, said, "ICMR is committed to ensuring that publicly funded research translates into products that improve health outcomes. Through initiatives such as Medical Innovations Patent Mitra, we are strengthening the pathway from scientific discovery to commercialization by fostering partnerships between researchers and industry. These technology transfers demonstrate the growing maturity of India's biomedical innovation ecosystem and represent another step towards achieving self-reliance in healthcare innovation." As India's apex biomedical research organization, ICMR has established an integrated innovation ecosystem that supports healthcare technologies across the innovation continuum—from discovery and intellectual property protection to clinical validation, regulatory facilitation and commercialization. Through Medical Innovations Patent Mitra, innovators receive structured support for patent filing, technology transfer and licensing, while MedTech Mitra facilitates regulatory guidance, clinical evaluation and market access for indigenous medical technologies. The licensing of these technologies reflects the growing strength of India's biomedical innovation ecosystem, where scientific excellence, strategic collaborations and industry partnerships are enabling affordable, high-quality healthcare solutions for India and the world. *** SR/GS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2286902) आगंतुक पटल  : 721 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Gujarati , Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali , Bengali-TR , Punjabi , Tamil , Telugu Ministry of Health and Family Welfare ICMR transfers three indigenous biomedical technologies to advance cancer and infectious disease solutions SHetA2 Anti-HPV candidate, two enteric vaccines among technologies transferred for further development Technology transfer brings government-funded research closer to affordable healthcare Medical Innovations Patent Mitra driving India's path to self-reliance in healthcare innovation: Secretary DHR and DG ICMR, Dr. Rajiv Bahl प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: DELAYED IMPLEMENTATION AND UTILISATION GAPS UNDER THE FAME-II ELECTRIC MOBILITY SCHEME
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Heavy Industries DELAYED IMPLEMENTATION AND UTILISATION GAPS UNDER THE FAME-II ELECTRIC MOBILITY SCHEME प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 JUL 2026 5:05PM by PIB Delhi The details of the schemes implemented by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) for the development of electric vehicles in the country along with provisions for charging stations are as under: Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles in India (FAME India) Scheme Phase-II : The Government implemented this scheme for a period of five years from 01.04.2019 to 31.03.2024 with a total budgetary support of ₹11,500 crore. The scheme provided demand incentive for e-2Ws, e-3Ws, e-4Ws and grant for e-buses and setting up of EV public charging stations (EV PCS). FAME-II has supported the sale of approximately 16.72 lakh electric vehicles, including e-2Ws, e-3Ws, and e-4Ws. In addition, 5,197 electric buses (e-buses) have been deployed under the Scheme as on 30.06.2026. Further, an amount of ₹912.50 crore was allocated under the Scheme for the establishment of EVPCS across the country. Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India (PLI-Auto): The Government notified this scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India, on 23.09.2021, for enhancing India's manufacturing capabilities for Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products, including EVs, with a budgetary outlay of ₹25,938 crore. Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage : The Government on 09.06.2021 notified the PLI  Scheme for manufacturing of ACC in the country with a budgetary outlay of ₹18,100 crore. The scheme aims to establish a competitive domestic manufacturing ecosystem for 50 GWh of ACC batteries. PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM EDRIVE) Scheme: This scheme with an outlay of ₹10,900 crore has been notified on 29.09.2024. This scheme supports incentivization of approximately 28.30 lakh electric vehicles (EVs) including e-2W, e-3W, e-Trucks, e-buses and e-Ambulances. Further, grant for EV public charging stations (EV PCS) and upgradation of testing agencies is also available under this scheme. An allocation of ₹4,391 crore has been made under the scheme for deployment of 14,028 e-buses out of which 13,800 e-buses have been allocated in seven cities having four million plus population viz. Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Pune and Surat. Further, 200 e-buses have been approved for Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir. ₹2,000 crore has been allocated for deployment of EV Public Charging Station on pan India basis. PM e-Bus Sewa-Payment Security Mechanism (PSM) Scheme : This Scheme notified on 28.10.2024, has an outlay of ₹3,435.33 crore and aims to support deployment of more than 38,000 electric buses. The objective of this scheme is to provide payment security to e-bus operators in case of default by Public Transport Authorities (PTAs). Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electric Passenger Cars in India (SPMEPCI) was notified on 15 th March, 2024 to promote the manufacturing of electric cars in India. This scheme requires applicants to invest a minimum of ₹4,150 crore and to achieve a minimum DVA of 25% at the end of the third year and DVA of 50% at the end of the fifth year. title: ASSESSMENT OF RARE EARTH PERMANENT MANAGEMENT SCHEME
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Heavy Industries ASSESSMENT OF RARE EARTH PERMANENT MANAGEMENT SCHEME प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 JUL 2026 5:04PM by PIB Delhi An assessment of Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM) demand in India was done by IREL (India) Limited, Defence Metallurgical Research Laboratory (DMRL) and Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC).  The estimated segment – wise requirement for REPM for the year 2030 is as under:- S. No. Sector Requirement in MTPA for the year 2030 1 Electric Vehicles (2/3/4 Wheelers) 3250 2 Industrial Motors for different applications 500 3 BLDC Fans 980 4 Smart Phones & Computers 600 5 Solar-powered Pumps 170 6 Elevators Motors and Escalator Motors 100 7 Other Applications (Consumer electronics, etc.) 820 8 Wind Turbine 1800 9 Total Consolidated Demand in India 8220 As on date, Geological Survey of India (GSI) has augmented cumulative Rare Earth Element (REE) ore resources totaling 767 million tonnes across the country, evaluated at different cut-off values and average grades since MMDR Amendment Act, 2015. While India possesses upstream capabilities in mining, separation and oxide refining, there is a notable gap in the industrial-scale midstream capabilities needed for oxide-to-metal, metal-to-alloy and alloy-to-magnet conversion. Due to this, India currently imports all its sintered NdFeB REPM demand for downstream applications. In order to bridge this gap, the Union Cabinet has approved the Scheme to Promote Manufacturing of Sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM) with a financial outlay of Rs. 7,280 Crore on 26 th November, 2025. The said scheme was notified on 15 th December, 2025. title: CYBERSECURITY VULNERABILITIES IN E-RICKSHAW BMS AND ROLE OF CERTIFICATION AGENCIES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Heavy Industries CYBERSECURITY VULNERABILITIES IN E-RICKSHAW BMS AND ROLE OF CERTIFICATION AGENCIES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 JUL 2026 5:03PM by PIB Delhi The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has received reports of safety concern involving electric three-wheelers (e-rickshaws). It has been reported that it is possible for unauthorized individuals to abruptly power off moving e-rickshaws by using a publicly available BMS mobile application. The issue lies in the Bluetooth module of the Battery Management System (BMS) chip, which is embedded in the battery module. The BMS commonly found in the low-cost e-rickshaws, have default or no credentials, which allows unauthorised users to connect and modify the settings and/or cut off the battery’s discharge, causing sudden vehicle shutdowns. CERT-In has identified the mobile apps which can be used to abruptly power-off batteries of erickshaws and reported to MeitY to remove the apps from application play stores. MHI has issued advisory for addressing Bluetooth BMS vulnerabilities in e-rickshaws to SIAM, ACMA Industry bodies and testing agencies. As per the information received from Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) cyber security regulations have not been framed in respect of E-rickshaw and E-kart. However, the Battery Safety Requirements for L-category EVs shall meet the standards prescribed in AIS 156 and Electric Power Train Safety shall comply with AIS 038 Rev. (2). The Government in the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways vide G.S.R. 503(E) dated 17th June, 2026 has published draft rules for approval of vehicles about cyber security in respect of vehicles of category L, M and N as per AIS- 189 and AIS- 190. Further, Rule 126 of the CMVR, 1989 mandates that every manufacturer or importer of a motor vehicle, including electric vehicles, shall submit the prototype to a testing agency notified under Rule 126. The testing agency issues a Type Approval Certificate certifying compliance with the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the CMVR, 1989. This information was given by the Minister of State for Heavy Industries, Shri Bhupathiraju Srinivasa Varma in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. ***** TPJ (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287127) आगंतुक पटल  : 77 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Heavy Industries CYBERSECURITY VULNERABILITIES IN E-RICKSHAW BMS AND ROLE OF CERTIFICATION AGENCIES प्रविष्टि तिथि:

The Ministry of Power issued the "Guidelines for Installation and Operation of Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure 2024," which outline standards for a connected and interoperable charging network, including battery swapping and charging stations. Setting up EV charging stations is an un-licensed activity, allowing private entrepreneurs to establish charging infrastructure more easily. Cars are supported under the PLI scheme for Automobile & Auto Components (PLI-Auto). Under the PLI Auto scheme, financial incentives of 13% to 18% were provided on determined (incremental) sales of AAT vehicles [including electric cars (e-4w)] to champion OEMs. An allocation of ₹4,391 crore has been made under PM E-DRIVE for deployment of 14,028 e-buses. A total of 13,800 e-buses have been allocated to 7 cities namely Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Pune and Surat. Tender process for selection of e-bus operators for these 13,800 e-buses has also concluded by 30.12.2025 (Phase I tender for 10,900 e-buses) and 27.05.2026 (Phase II tender for 2,900 e-buses). As on 30.06.2026, Letters of Award (LoAs) have been issued by Ahmedabad, Hyderabad and Surat. The Concession Agreements (CAs) have been signed by Hyderabad for 915 e-buses out of 2,000 e-buses allocated to Hyderabad and by Surat for 600 e-buses. Besides this 200 e-buses have been approved for deployment in hilly terrain in Jammu & Kashmir. Convergence Energy Services Limited (CESL) and the Ministry of Heavy Industries is holding regular consultations and reviews with the State Government and STUs for faster deployment of these buses. The scheme provided demand incentive for e-2Ws, e-3Ws, e-4Ws and grant for e-buses and setting up of EV public charging stations (EV PCS). FAME-II has supported the sale of approximately 16.72 lakh electric vehicles, including e-2Ws, e-3Ws, and e-4Ws. In addition, 5,197 electric buses (e-buses) have been deployed under the Scheme as on 30.06.2026. Further, an amount of ₹912.50 crore was allocated under the Scheme for the establishment of EVPCS across the country. Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage: The Government on 09.06.2021 notified the PLI  Scheme for manufacturing of ACC in the country with a budgetary outlay of ₹18,100 crore. The scheme aims to establish a competitive domestic manufacturing ecosystem for 50 GWh of ACC batteries. PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM EDRIVE) Scheme: This scheme with an outlay of ₹10,900 crore has been notified on 29.09.2024. This scheme supports incentivization of approximately 28.30 lakh electric vehicles (EVs) including e-2W, e-3W, e-Trucks, e-buses and e-Ambulances. Further, EV public charging stations (EV PCS) and upgradation of testing agencies is also included in this scheme. An allocation of ₹4,391 crore has been made under the scheme for deployment of 14,028 e-buses out of which 13,800 e-buses have been allocated in seven cities having four million plus population viz. Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Pune and Surat. Further, 200 e-buses have been approved for hilly terrain in the state of Jammu & Kashmir. Moreover, ₹2,000 crore has been allocated for deployment of EV PCS on pan India basis. PM e-Bus Sewa-Payment Security Mechanism (PSM) Scheme : This Scheme notified on 28.10.2024, has an outlay of ₹3,435.33 crore and aims to support deployment of more than 38,000 electric buses. The objective of this scheme is to provide payment security to e-bus operators in case of default by Public Transport Authorities (PTAs). Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electric Passenger Cars in India (SPMEPCI) was notified on 15th March, 2024 to promote the manufacturing of electric cars in India. This scheme requires applicants to invest a minimum of ₹4,150 crore and to achieve a minimum DVA of 25% at the end of the third year and DVA of 50% at the end of the fifth year. Further, following initiatives have also been taken up by the Government of India to increase the use of electric vehicles in the country: – i.             GST on electric vehicles and chargers/ charging stations for electric vehicles has been reduced to 5%. ii.  Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (MoRTH) announced that battery-operated vehicles will be given green license plates and be exempted from permit requirements. iii. MoRTH issued advisory to states to waive road tax on EVs, which in turn will help reduce the initial cost of EVs. title: TRAFFICKING OF NARCOTICS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs TRAFFICKING OF NARCOTICS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                21 JUL 2026 4:08PM by PIB Delhi Government has taken various steps to check and prevent the illicit trafficking of narcotics. The important steps are as under: - (i) Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), Drug Law Enforcement Agencies (DLEAs) and State Police, are actively engaged in enforcement activity under the Narcotics Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985. These concerted efforts have resulted in significant achievements in term of drug seizures, registration of cases, arrests, disposal of seized drugs, destruction of illicit cultivation, financial investigations and preventive detention under Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (PITNDPS) Act, 1988. (ii)     To address the challenge of illicit drug trafficking & abuse of drugs, Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026-2029) has been released on 26.06.2026, which lays down a 3-year road map with clear priorities and time bound targets to be achieved by various stakeholders to control drugs with ‘whole-of-government’ & ‘whole-of-society’ approach. (iii) Established a 4-tier Narco-Coordination Centre (NCORD) mechanism for ensuring better coordination between Central & State Drug Law Enforcement Agencies and other stake holders in the field of controlling drug trafficking and drug abuse in India. (iv)    To monitor the investigation of significant and important drug cases including cases of narco-terrorism, a Joint Coordination Committee (JCC ) with DG, NCB as its Chairman has been set up. (v)     All DGPs of States/UTs have been requested for sensitization of beat constables, field officers and SHOs regarding Red Flag Indicators (RFI) and emerging threats relating to clandestine manufacturing of synthetic drugs, particularly Mephedrone and ATS. (vi)    Financial investigations and effective implementation of the PITNDPS is being regularly emphasized at forums viz. NCORD, JCC, Regional Conference for dismantling and weakening of organized synthetic drug trafficking networks. (vii)   Comprehensive guideline on financial investigation, facilitating systematic identification, tracing and attachment of proceeds of crime have been issued. (viii)  For the capacity building of Drug Law Enforcement Officers and Agencies, NCB organizes workshops/ seminars/ training programmes. NCB is regularly conducting specialised training programmes on investigation of clandestine laboratories and precursor chemical diversion in collaboration with the US-DEA, with participation of officers from Central Agencies and State DLEAs. (ix)    India holds regular Director General (DG) Level/Bilateral talks on drug related matters with countries such as Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Singapore, United States of America (USA). (x)     NCB has strengthened international cooperation in drug control through bilateral agreements with 27 countries and MoUs with 19 countries. To strengthen NCB, the following steps have been taken:- i. Regional offices have been increased from 03 to 07 by addition of 04 Regional offices at Amritsar, Guwahati, Chennai and Ahmedabad. Zonal offices have been increased from 13 to 30, across the Country by addition of 05 new Zonal offices at Gorakhpur (Uttar Pradesh), Siliguri (West Bengal), Agartala (Tripura), Itanagar (Arunachal Pradesh) and Raipur (Chhattisgarh) and by upgradation of 12 existing Sub-zones as Zones. Approval has been accorded recently for establishment of Six (06) new Zonal Offices at Port Blair (Andaman & Nicobar Islands), Dimapur (Nagaland), Aizawl (Mizoram), Shimla (Himachal Pradesh), Shillong (Meghalaya) and Gangtok (Sikkim). In addition, 10 Field offices have been approved and operationalized. 568 new posts have been created in the sanctioned strength of NCB. In-principle approval for the establishment of a dedicated Directorate of Prosecution within the Narcotics Control Bureau has been accorded. Additionally, 36 prosecutors have been engaged at Regional and Zonal offices to add value to the effective prosecution efforts.
